extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for the NIA F32 (NRSA) individual fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting a National Institute on Aging (NIA) F32 Individual Postdoctoral Fellowship (NRSA) application, including eligibility, deadlines, budget/stipend rules, and component length limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility – career stage and research field
rubrics_metrics.description: The F32 (PA-25-423) is available to postdoctoral researchers doing research in the aging field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be at the postdoctoral career stage and conducting aging-related research consistent with NIA's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / residency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All F32 recipients must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents at the time of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who are not U.S. citizens/permanent residents are not eligible; verify status before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum award duration and prior T32 support offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdocs may receive up to 3 years of NRSA postdoctoral research support (F32). Postdocs who have not been supported by a postdoctoral T32 may request the full 3 years. Those who have been supported by a postdoctoral T32 should subtract their years of T32 support and request 1 or 2 years of F32 funding accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate requested F32 years by subtracting prior T32 postdoctoral support years; consult your program director to determine T32 funding history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application receipt dates and review/award cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH NRSA fellowships are awarded in three cycles each year with specified application due dates: April 8, August 8, December 8. Initial review and earliest possible award start months differ by cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan submission according to the cycle schedule: Cycle 1 (due Apr 8 → initial review Jun/Jul → earliest award Dec), Cycle 2 (due Aug 8 → initial review Oct/Nov → earliest award Apr), Cycle 3 (due Dec 8 → initial review Feb/Mar → earliest award Jul).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Abstract length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract — 30 lines of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the abstract concise and within the 30-line limit; follow SF424 (R&R) Application Guide details for formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Project Narrative length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Narrative — 3 sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a brief, plain-language statement of the project's relevance to public health in three sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Candidate Biosketch length limit and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate Biosketch — 5 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A biosketch contains a CV, personal statement, and description of past research experience; follow NIH biosketch format and page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Sponsor Biosketch length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor Biosketch — 5 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor(s) must supply an NIH-format biosketch within the 5-page limit describing qualifications to mentor the fellow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Candidate Goals, Preparedness, and Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate Goals, Preparedness, and Potential — 3 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the candidate's training goals, preparedness for the proposed research and career development potential within the 3-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Training Activities and Timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Activities and Timelines — 3 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed planned training activities, schedules, and timelines for accomplishing training and research objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Research Training Project Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Training Project Specific Aims — 1 page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the specific aims of the research training project succinctly on one page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Research Training Project Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Training Project Strategy — 6 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the scientific and training approach, methods, preliminary data, and rationale within the 6-page strategy limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Sponsor(s) Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor(s) Commitment — 6 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document mentor commitment, training plan, resources, and institutional support within the 6-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants — 6 pages (collective or per category as required by application forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide letters that document planned collaborations, roles, resource commitments, and any other contributions; stay within the allowed page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component: Reference letters requirements and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: 3–5 Reference Letters — 2 pages each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide between three and five reference letters, each no more than two pages. For postdoctoral grant applications, a reference letter from your predoctoral thesis advisor is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch definition and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: A biosketch is a document containing a CV, personal statement, and description of past research experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH biosketch format and content expectations; use the 5-page limit for candidate and sponsor biosketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend schedule (2025) by years of postdoctoral experience
rubrics_metrics.description: F32 stipends depend on years of postdoctoral experience. Listed examples (2025): 0 years $62,232; 1 year $62,652; 2 years $63,120; 3 years $65,640; 4 years $67,824; 5 years $70,344; 6 years $72,960; 7+ years $75,564.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the applicant's counted postdoctoral experience to determine stipend level; check NOT-OD-25-105 for updated budget levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition and fees caps and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum Tuition & Fees — $4,500 (general cap), with payment allowed up to 60% of institutional tuition or $4,500, whichever is less. Exception: postdocs enrolled in a degree-granting program may have tuition/fees paid up to 60% of institutional tuition or $16,000, whichever is less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 60%-of-institution-or-dollar-cap rule based on enrollment status (degree vs. non-degree). Confirm institutional tuition figures and which cap applies to the fellow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Allowance amount and permissible uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional Allowance — $12,400 (per year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional Allowance may be used to cover expenses such as health insurance, research supplies, equipment, books, and travel to scientific meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Childcare costs allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each fellow may request $3,000 per year to defray childcare costs from a licensed provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who need childcare support may request this amount; see FAQs on Childcare Costs for details and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRSA payback obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA postdoctoral fellows incur a payback obligation that could affect F32 recipients who complete less than 2 years of their award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand payback rules before accepting partial awards or leaving the award before two years; consult FAQs about the payback obligation for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of research topic for NIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether an F32 research topic is appropriate for the NIA by consulting the list of currently funded NIA F32s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncertain, submit a one-page overview of specific aims to NIATraining@mail.nih.gov for feedback; a program official will respond and advise on fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application instructions and required forms reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed instructions for each application part can be found in the SF424 (R&R) Application Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow SF424 (R&R) Application Guide and NIH policies (including updated fellowship review/application changes effective Jan 25, 2025) when preparing your submission.
